text:
maya: :rotating_light: heads up — seeing a sudden spike in LBA remap churn on ap-south1 local-nvme pool, started ~10m ago. Metadata syncs are spiking and several GPU attach requests are timing out (~15-25s). Impacting non-prod and a couple Dedicated lanes.
ben: logs? any node list?
maya: checking — main flare on gnode-97, gnode-102, gnode-118. sample dmesg: 
```
[  123.456789] nvme0: remap table growth: refs=1024 -> 8192, metadata_sync=EIO
[  124.001234] nvme: metadata write failure, retrying
```
ashley: ack. that pattern looks like remap metadata amplification — cleaner/scrub overlap? did we just push a scrub cadence change last night?
kai: confirmed — scrub cadence bumped in ap-south1 at 02:10 UTC. scrub-controller logs show concurrent runs. suggestion: throttle janitor concurrency to 2 for ap-south1 nodes for next 2h.
ben: agree. temporary mitigation: annotate nodes to limit cleaner pods. example: `kubectl annotate node gnode-97 warehouse.redwood/cleaner-max=2` — will need a k8s rollout for scrub-controller confmap too.
ops-lead: what's the SLA impact? any Dedicated customer routes seeing errors?
maya: two Dedicated job attachments retried, one failed and fell back to lower tier. Not widespread but visible. Ops on standby.
sre-bot: ALERT ap-south1 nvme.remap_rate > 600/s for 12 nodes — incident_id=INC-20260323-0123
ashley: quick cost note — if we move GPU workloads cross-region to us-west for remediation, estimate additional egress + spot churn ~ $1.2k/day. prefer local throttle first.
kai: plan: 1) set cleaner concurrency=2 via confmap (5m deploy), 2) annotate the top 10 hot nodes to pause scrubs, 3) back off KV-cache compaction task for 1h. Canary on gnode-97 then batch.
ben: pushing a small confmap change now. I'll also add a temporary feature-flag to skip scrub-on-attach.
maya: executing node annotations for gnode-97/102/118/121/130 now.
ashley: also proposing a short firmware rollback window for the nvme controller group on those nodes — last firmware pushed 3 days ago, might correlate. rollback would be intrusive. prefer throttle+backoff first.
ops-lead: agree with Ashley but postpone firmware until after scrub cadence proven. communicate to Dedicated customers flagged in the incident.
ben: confmap applied, scrub-controller pods restarted, annotates landed. monitoring.
(2m later) maya: remap rate dropped ~70%, attach latencies recovering to baseline. :thumbsup:
kai: I'll open a follow-up RFC to adjust scrub schedule heuristics and add rate-limiters to remap growth path. link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-storage-remap-guardrails
ashley: filing a ticket to track firmware correlation: STORAGE-789.
ops-lead: good work — keep monitoring for 2h, then we'll lift annotations. postmortem if we see recurrence.
maya: will update status page and slack incident channel. closing this thread once we verify stability. :eyes:
